name: hivemind
description: Shared, versioned knowledge graph + artifact store + tool registry that REPLACES local agent memory: read it before any work, persist all work into it.

server_url.title: Hivemind server URL
server_url.description: Your Hivemind server, used as ${server_url}/mcp. Give the SERVER ROOT (http://<host>:8787). On the root every call must pass project= — reads as well as writes — so a forgotten argument is refused instead of landing in whatever the URL named; it needs a token minted with --user. The project comes from the session pin: the SessionStart hook exports it as HIVEMIND_PROJECT beside HIVEMIND_SERVER_URL, and the live guide and the hivemind CLI build /p/<project>/guide and /p/<project>/blobs from the two (each variable is only a fallback — one you exported yourself wins). A project path (http://<host>:8787/p/default) still works and keeps the old fallback behaviour: that URL names the project, so a call omitting project= acts in it, and the shell consumers use it verbatim.

api_token.title: API token
api_token.description: Bearer token from `hivemind-admin mint-token --user <you> --device <machine>`, kept in the server's identities.json. It names a person, which is what puts an author on your writes, and it reaches every project that person may access. An older per-project token (the server's tokens.json) still works, but only with the project-path form of the URL above — on the server root it gets a 401, because it is pinned to a project that URL has not named. The SessionStart hook also exports it as HIVEMIND_TOKEN for the session's Bash calls, so the live guide and the hivemind CLI can authenticate; that file is narrowed to 0600 before the token is written to it.
